description: GhanaMining-Sat is a labelled satellite image set for detecting artisanal and small-scale gold mining (galamsey) in Ghana. The DataCite record says it holds 300 manually labelled 256 by 256 pixel patches cut from Sentinel-2 imagery over three mining regions, Prestea, Tarkwa and Obuasi, with 244 mining and 56 non-mining patches, stratified train and test splits, baseline ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0 models with 93 percent accuracy and a cross-site test averaging 76 percent on unseen locations, plus README, metadata and citation files. Version 1.0.0 was published on 17 October 2025 by Eleazer Henry Danso on Zenodo, downloadable and free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is three districts in south-western Ghana. Caveats: the sample is small, the page notes that legal status needs cross-checking with mining permit databases, and image dates and the exact band set are not stated on the page read. For simulation it helps train models that map informal mining, so the mapped sites can become hazard sources or exposure layers near water intakes, roads and farmland. Related catalogue records include the IPIS artisanal mining sites open data, Mapping Mining Areas in the Tropics and the WAPHA global metal mines database.
